newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech stocks close lower, led by IPB, Komercni.
newsitem.headline: Czech stocks close lower, led by IPB, Komercni.

text.p: The Czech PX50 index fell further on Wednesday, led down by losses to shares in banks IPB and Komercni, and dealers said the market could go still lower on Friday after the May 1 holiday.
The PX50 fell two points, or 0.38 percent, to 529.3.
IPB fell 16 crowns to 304 after two senior bank officials were charged with fraud on Tuesday. Komercni closed 39 crowns lower at 2,186 after it reported lower first quarter profits.
SPT Telecom also reported lower first quarter profits and eased 35 to 3,270.

"For the moment, since I do not see any positive reaction to these results coming from abroad ... I think the only way for the market is trading sideways or coming off even further," said INB Barings trader Radim Bajgar.
Dealers said domestic market makers had been marking prices down and that there was little interest even in blue chips from foreign investors.
Wood & Co trader Andrea Sarancova said foreign investors were put off by the lack of transparency in the market but that the IPB probe could eventually have a positive impact.
Bajgar said the market was still waiting for details of the substance of the IPB investigations.
Power generator CEZ, due to report quarterly results on Friday, fell six to 964 while Ceska Sporitelna closed six higher at 317 crowns.
Prague financial markets are closed on Thursday but reopen on Friday.
